correctness.rationale: Fix \(0<a<b<3a\), \(0<c<c_*\). Exact coefficient arithmetic verifies \(\dot f=kf\) for the complete five-variable canonical system. Substitution gives the two branch velocities \(\dot x=xR(4cR\pm m)\); the derivative \(F'(x)=s(x-x_*)/(4R^3)\) proves the unique interior minimum and both orientations. Exact branch integration yields the unrescaled period; its positive derivative gives global monotonicity and trigonometric partial fractions give the zero-parameter limit. The quadratic expansion at \(x_*\) produces the sharp \((c_*-c)^{-1/2}\) coefficient. A tail-controlled rescaling establishes the standard Cauchy occupation law. The stdlib checker proves the global cofactor polynomial identity and gives independent finite quadrature comparisons; the global limit and weak convergence are proved analytically rather than inferred from finite tests.

originality.rationale: The source paper Gasull–Giacomini, arXiv:2210.15803v1 (public 2022-10-27; primary MSC 34C07), and earlier Yablonskii literature already establish the classical invariant quartic and parameter range, which are credited. Relevant full-text sections of that 2022 uniqueness paper, the 2019 Cremona/Qin equivalence paper and a 2005 cofactor/hyperbolicity paper were inspected; none states the combined original-time period formula, sharp coefficient and scaled Cauchy law in the examined material. Cremona equivalence entails a nonconstant time change and does not itself imply original-time measurements. Targeted source, alias and discriminant searches identified no covering statement in the accessible records. The 1966 and 2004 original full texts could not be inspected completely, so absolute historical priority is not asserted.

value.rationale: The known Yablonskii oval is a natural algebraic limit cycle; original-time period and occupation are fundamental observables not determined by its existence, counting, geometric equivalence, or hyperbolicity. Strict all-parameter response, the exact arrest coefficient, and a universal Cauchy concentration law distinguish a fixed-size oval developing a velocity zero from orbit shrinkage. This is a motivated dynamical classification across a natural continuous parameter family, not a renaming, an arbitrary finite slice or a numerical gain.
